correctness.rationale: The generator and unweighted norms are explicit, n is even, and all time/asymptotic quantifiers are stated. A finite generating-function computation yields a strict central maximizing column and an exact binomial-tail integral; differentiating proves monotonicity. Hamming lumping plus a binomial absolute-deviation identity proves the infinity derivative norm. A binomial local limit theorem with a uniform boundary envelope establishes the sharp sqrt(n) infinity limit, and a separate exact central-column derivative at t=(log n)/4 proves the sqrt(n) log n l1 lower bound. All critical formulas were also checked against independent finite Poisson-uniformization calculations (427 comparisons). The lower bound is not misrepresented as an exact l1 asymptotic.

value.rationale: The semigroup is a canonical finitely lumped reversible diffusion. The exact central-column norm measures a naturally motivated stability functional under unweighted perturbations of aggregate states, and its sharp sqrt(n) long-time amplification is nontrivial. The proved log(n) gap for time-weighted derivatives between l1 counting and l∞ is a qualitative structural endpoint phenomenon inaccessible from spectral locations or the reversible stationary-weighted contractivity statement alone. It motivates norm choices when lumping high-dimensional state spaces.
